hypothesis: A test-body-only compiler region hides failures in the imported binding or helper that the test newly uses. Follow symbol-linked local declarations before subtracting baseline diagnostics.
cohort: All 24 original TypeScript parents from the frozen all17 source cohort, exactly the round23 cohort.
method: Resolve identifier symbols from selected test ASTs; follow declarations in the same source file; retain individual imported bindings and their module literals; compare source-control and generated diagnostic multisets.
tests: Four synthetic compiler tests pass. They cover a missing export in a shared import declaration, a newly used invalid helper, unrelated unused broken dependencies, and closure budget exhaustion. The first test also confirms the old worker misses the import error.
limitations: The closure stays within the test source file. It does not analyze all imported implementation bodies.
Compiler types can be wrong in the submitted implementation. Diagnostics supply counterevidence and do not establish oracle truth.
No detector output or task-level score changes in this component.
decision: Retain dependency-aware checking as a construction diagnostic. It detects one missed import error. It does not justify any oracle or improve the measured detector score.
